inspection_summary: Inspected all 218 lines. The source develops one connected argument: xi is introduced as an entire completion with the nonreal zeta zeros and a reflection symmetry; zero-free half-planes force horizontal growth of Hadamard zero factors; a partial-sum regrouping controls the sole decreasing exponential factor; and the resulting monotonicity is equivalent to RH through zero exclusion and the functional equation. Displayed formulas have extraction damage but the accepted mechanisms are recoverable from adjoining prose, with formula-level reuse flagged for scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Xi as an entire completion with reflection symmetry
accepted_units.why_material: The passage relates zeta's nonreal-zero problem to an entire function: the added factors cancel the pole and real zeros, so xi retains precisely the nonreal zeta zeros, while xi(1-s)=xi(s) supplies the symmetry used later.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the zeta/RH setup because the cancellation claim and the meaning of xi zeros would otherwise require reconstruction; page-boundary and classification text inside the span are incidental.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The xi product at lines 44-50 has broken superscript/fraction layout; the cancellation, entire-function, zero-set, and functional-equation claims are clear in prose at lines 62-69, but formula-exact reuse should consult the scan.

accepted_units.title: Zero-free half-planes force horizontal monotonicity of xi modulus
accepted_units.why_material: The theorem converts absence of xi zeros in an open right or left half-plane into strict increase or decrease of modulus on every contained horizontal half-line, with the region outside the critical strip given as an immediate instance.
accepted_units.context_note: The local conventions make monotonicity strict and half-lines endpoint-free; the later corollary and proof are intentionally separate units.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: the semantic claim is stated in prose; the extracted inequalities in the example are legible.

accepted_units.title: RH as two-sided horizontal monotonicity about the critical line
accepted_units.why_material: The corollary gives an operational equivalence: strict horizontal monotonicity on either side excludes zeros there, and the functional equation supplies the reflected side; conversely RH makes both open half-planes zero-free so the theorem applies.
accepted_units.context_note: The critical line and functional equation were established at lines 42-43 and 67-69; this span contains the full equivalence statement and proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The extracted one-half bounds appear as spaced digits at lines 92-93, but their role as the previously defined critical-line boundary is recoverable from the checked source context.

accepted_units.title: Reduce monotonicity to factors in the Hadamard product
accepted_units.why_material: The proof reduces the left-half-plane statement by the functional equation, fixes a horizontal line inside a zero-free right half-plane, and changes representation to xi's Hadamard product, isolating the negative real exponential constant B from zero-indexed factors.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the setup required by every subsequent factorwise and compensating argument; the page marker at lines 106-110 is incidental.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed Hadamard product and explicit value of B are layout-damaged at lines 119-126; their factor roles are recoverable from lines 116-123 and the later prose, but exact exponents/constants require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Zero exclusion turns each linear factor into increasing distance
accepted_units.why_material: Because every zero lies on or left of the half-plane boundary while the moving point stays to its right, horizontal motion increases its distance from each zero and hence increases the modulus of each linear Hadamard factor.
accepted_units.context_note: Uses the fixed zero-free half-plane and horizontal half-line introduced at lines 111-114.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The final quotient notation at lines 136-138 is fragmented, but the distance argument and monotonic conclusion are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Hadamard exponential factors are non-decreasing along the half-line
accepted_units.why_material: Writing a zero as beta+i gamma makes the modulus exponent affine in the horizontal coordinate with nonnegative coefficient beta, so each exponential zero factor is non-decreasing; strict increase is noted as unnecessary.
accepted_units.context_note: This complements the strictly increasing linear factors and deliberately proves only the strength needed for the product argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed modulus computation at lines 144-147 is typographically scrambled, but beta>=0 and the non-decreasing conclusion are explicit at lines 141-150.

accepted_units.title: Regroup the negative exponential prefactor through zero partial sums
accepted_units.why_material: The sole obstruction is the decreasing factor from B<0. An alternate series for -B yields partial sums S_N with -(B+S_N)>0 tending to zero; combining exponential factors then rewrites xi as a finite zero product, an infinite increasing tail, and a residual factor whose decay can be made arbitrarily small.
accepted_units.context_note: The span includes the B-series identity, definition and limiting behavior of S_N, finite product P_N, and the regrouped Hadamard product needed for the closing derivative argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several conjugation bars, fractions, exponents, and product bounds are damaged in lines 156-186. The regrouping mechanism and limiting sign are recoverable from lines 151-154, 162-180, but formula-exact use requires scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A vanishing residual decay yields strict local growth at every point
accepted_units.why_material: After the finite and infinite zero products are known to increase, the remaining factor f_N has positive derivative when a positive distance ratio exceeds -(B+S_N). At any chosen point, zero exclusion makes that ratio positive and the residual tends to zero, so some N gives positivity on a neighborhood; arbitrariness of the point and horizontal line proves the theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: Begins with the factorwise conclusion from the regrouped product and retains the complete choice-of-N, neighborhood, and arbitrary-point closure.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The definition of f_N is heavily layout-damaged at lines 192-200, but the derivative criterion, convergence used to choose N, neighborhood conclusion, and theorem closure are explicit at lines 201-209; scan verification is required before reusing the exact formula.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Horizontal monotonicity as a zero-exclusion certificate
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: For this xi setting, functional symmetry and the zero-free-half-plane monotonicity theorem turn one-sided horizontal modulus behavior into an equivalent criterion excluding off-critical zeros.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The equivalence is conditional on the paper's xi-specific theorem and symmetry; the source does not establish a generic criterion for arbitrary entire functions.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Factorwise growth plus vanishing-obstruction compensation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A product representation can prove strict modulus growth even with one decreasing global factor: isolate growing zero factors, rewrite the decay as a residual tail tending to zero, and choose the truncation so a positive local distance derivative dominates at each point.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The mechanism here relies on the cited B-series identity, the source's constraints on zero real parts, and formula-damaged displays that require scan checking for exact reuse.
